page.layout: One printed page (p. 182), single text column, with a headline block and epigraph above the column. A small marginal "6." stands at the top left. The narrow strip at the right edge belongs to the neighbouring page and is not transcribed. The catchword "porrò" stands at the bottom right.

main_text.l: PRÆLECTIO SEPTIMA.
De Obligatione Legum Humanarum
ex parte Causæ Efficientis.
PROV. VIII. 15.

l.i: Per me Reges regnant, & Legum conditores

main_text.l: I. DE Legum Humanarum Obligatione egi-
mus superiore Termino: cum in
genere, Quod nimirum Leges Humanæ
rite constitutæ obligent subditorum
conscientias ad obediendum: tum etiam in speciali,
quoad illa dubia quæ ad Causam Materialem pro-
pius pertinere videbantur. Quatenus scilicet ob-
ligent latæ Leges, primò de rebus impossibilibu-
s; secundò, de possibilibus sed multum onerosis; ter-
tiò, de necessariis; quartò, de illicitis & inhone-
stis; quintò, de malis permittendis; sextò, de re-
bus mediis & adiaphoris in communi; septimò,
de ritibus Ecclesiasticis in speciali. In quibus omni-
bus eorum quæ dicta sunt, (ne, dum singula re-
peto, molestus sim,) summa huc redit: obligari
subditos ad parendum Legibus Justis, ad paren-
dum injustis non obligari; juxta quod in Textu
propositò exigit à Legum conditoribus Salomon, ut
non nisi quæ justa sunt decernant. Pergendum
porrò

page.notes: The "6." in the left margin stands high on the page, above the headline block; I placed it at the start of the first paragraph. The faint lines above the rule at the top are show-through from the reverse side and are omitted. "in speciali" at the line end is partly obscured by the next line, so the italic tail is uncertain. The running head is omitted because the page opens a division. The word porrò is the catchword and is not repeated in the text.
